instructions: Human-reviewed ASM/SPEC. SPEC is interface-only; ASM is world/shared.

decompositions.loss: The owner's everyday driving video and face embeddings are retained or reused after an authorized search ends.
decompositions.req: After an authorized search expires, people and vehicles recorded by the owner's dashcam are not identifiable from anything retained for ChildFind.

assumptions.text: Owners understand and can refuse enrollment in ChildFind before any search photo is applied to their footage.
assumptions.why_fragile: Dark-pattern opt-in and OEM-installed defaults are common.

assumptions.text: When a search ends, every copy of embeddings and crops derived from this car is actually deleted, including contractor caches.
assumptions.why_fragile: Contractor stacks like Rekognition often retain artifacts for debugging.

assumptions.text: A paired phone is not silently backing up raw clips to a personal cloud the owner forgot about.
assumptions.why_fragile: Phone OS backups are outside the dashcam company's control.

specifications.text: On search expiry, delete on-device search photos, embeddings, and queued sighting-reports and emit a deletion-complete status.
On expiry, send a revoke message to every enrolled device and contractor endpoint that previously received that search-id.
Do not upload raw video for ChildFind; if a clip is sent, send only the still attached to an explicit sighting-report.

decompositions.loss: The owner receives an unexpected cellular bill because ChildFind uploaded video through their phone.
decompositions.req: The owner is not billed for cellular data used by ChildFind beyond a limit they accepted in advance.

assumptions.text: The phone's cellular path is the only way a queued report leaves the car, so byte volume on that path equals user-visible cost.
assumptions.why_fragile: OEM telematics or Wi-Fi at home may carry traffic the user does not attribute to ChildFind.

assumptions.text: The owner notices and can act on an in-app data budget before the carrier bills them.
assumptions.why_fragile: Carrier bills lag; many users never open the companion app.

assumptions.text: Wi-Fi hotspots used for upload are free or already paid.
assumptions.why_fragile: Captive-portal Wi-Fi can still meter or fail over to cellular.

specifications.text: Count ChildFind uplink bytes and stop cellular uploads when the user-set budget is reached, emitting a budget-exceeded status.
Prefer Wi-Fi and USB offload; mark reports as cellular-eligible only if the phone app has advertised remaining budget.
Show a pre-enrollment estimate of worst-case bytes per search-day given the local search frequency.

decompositions.loss: A ChildFind match notification distracts the driver and contributes to a crash.
decompositions.req: While the vehicle is moving, the driver is not prompted to inspect a possible-match image.

assumptions.text: The companion app can reliably know whether the vehicle is in motion from the dashcam or car speed signal.
assumptions.why_fragile: Bluetooth dropouts and aftermarket installs may not see speed.

assumptions.text: Passengers, not drivers, are the ones holding the phone when a prompt appears.
assumptions.why_fragile: The driver is often the only occupant.

assumptions.text: A sound or HUD flash is not enough to take the driver's eyes off the road.
assumptions.why_fragile: Any salient alert can still cause a glance.

specifications.text: Suppress match-preview UI and audible alerts whenever the last speed sample is above a parked threshold.
Do not display match images on any in-vehicle screen; only queue a silent sighting-report.
If a human review is required, route thumbnails to the non-profit reviewer interface, not to the moving driver.

decompositions.loss: After a child is found near the owner's route, the owner is blamed or sued for not reporting.
decompositions.req: An owner who had the device powered and enrolled is not treated as having a personal duty to have noticed the child.

assumptions.text: Courts and the public distinguish automated search from a human who saw the child.
assumptions.why_fragile: Headlines will not.

assumptions.text: Enrollment terms are presented before first use and retained.
assumptions.why_fragile: OEM-installed units may never show terms to the driver.

assumptions.text: Logs exist that show whether a search-alert was even on the device that day.
assumptions.why_fragile: Offline devices cannot prove they never received the alert.

specifications.text: Record per-device whether a search-alert was delivered, acknowledged, and whether any sighting-report was emitted.
Display that ChildFind is automated matching, not a request that the driver watch the road for a face.
Keep a tamper-evident log of search-id active windows and power state.

decompositions.loss: Always-on matching drains the battery or fills storage so the dashcam is dead when a crash happens.
decompositions.req: The dashcam continues to record a crash loop even when a ChildFind search is active.

assumptions.text: The unit is on vehicle power whenever the car is moving.
assumptions.why_fragile: Parking-mode battery packs are common.

assumptions.text: Person detection is cheap enough that crash-loop writes still keep up.
assumptions.why_fragile: Low-end models cannot run both.

assumptions.text: Owners will plug the camera back in after a low-battery shutdown.
assumptions.why_fragile: Many will not.

specifications.text: Treat crash-loop recording as a higher-priority write path than person-matching; drop matching when free space or voltage is below a reserved threshold.
Expose a power-state sample to the phone app when matching is shed.
If matching is shed, emit a search-degraded status so coordinators do not assume coverage.

decompositions.loss: Someone uses a fake 'missing child' enrollment to reconstruct the owner's routine from sighting metadata.
decompositions.req: A person who is not the subject of a bona fide, authority-backed search cannot obtain a trail of where the owner's car has been.

assumptions.text: Only authorities/non-profit can create a search-id, and they vet the requester.
assumptions.why_fragile: Legal details are explicitly unsettled in the scenario.

assumptions.text: Sighting-reports are not visible to the requester, only to the coordinating unit.
assumptions.why_fragile: Product pressure will be to give parents a live map.

assumptions.text: A search photo of an adult cannot be submitted under a child-search type.
assumptions.why_fragile: Nothing in the current legal process prevents this.

specifications.text: Accept new search-ids only from authenticated authority/non-profit accounts, not from end-user accounts.
Do not return sighting GPS to the original requester account; only to the coordinating-unit inbox.
Reject search packets whose metadata mark the subject as 18+ or whose photo fails a child-age gate.

decompositions.loss: The child remains missing even though they walked through a participating camera's view.
decompositions.req: If a missing child is physically visible in the field of view of a participating dashcam during an authorized search, the coordinating law-enforcement unit learns of that co-location while the child is still in the same local area.

assumptions.text: The dashcam is powered and the lens is unobstructed whenever the vehicle is on a public road.
assumptions.why_fragile: Parking-mode off, dirty lenses, and winter covers are common.

assumptions.text: The child's face or other distinctive appearance is not fully covered for the entire time they are in view.
assumptions.why_fragile: Abductors adapt once the system is known; weather gear hides faces.

assumptions.text: Within a short interval after the child is in view, the dashcam or paired phone obtains a network path that can deliver a small report.
assumptions.why_fragile: The product has no native Internet; cars park far from phones.

assumptions.text: The search packet contains a photograph that still resembles the child's current appearance.
assumptions.why_fragile: Children change clothes, hair, and even face shape; photos may be years old.

assumptions.text: Operators read inbound sighting notices rather than discarding them as noise.
assumptions.why_fragile: False-positive floods train operators to ignore the channel.

specifications.text: On receiving a search-alert (photo, search-id, geographic scope, expiry), store it until expiry and forward it to the paired dashcam.
For each in-scope person crop, output a match_score against the search photo.
When match_score exceeds the configured threshold, emit a sighting-report containing search-id, timestamp, GPS sample, and a cropped still.
If no radio is up, queue the sighting-report until the next successful Bluetooth/Wi-Fi/USB session or until search expiry.
On ingesting a sighting-report, present it in the coordinating-unit inbox with map pin and still, without requiring a second model pass that can drop it.

decompositions.loss: A public or in-app alert warns an abductor, who relocates the child before officers arrive.
decompositions.req: An abductor traveling with the child does not receive a real-time notice that a nearby camera just matched the child.

assumptions.text: Drivers do not get a push that names the child and shows 'match nearby' on a lock screen.
assumptions.why_fragile: Marketing will want visible 'you helped' moments.

assumptions.text: The abductor is not also a enrolled ChildFind user who receives the same search-alert photo.
assumptions.why_fragile: Anyone can buy a dashcam.

assumptions.text: Officers can intercept without a public crowd converging.
assumptions.why_fragile: Amber-style publicity is the default mental model.

specifications.text: Do not display the search photo or 'match nearby' to the driver; only a generic 'search active in region' state if anything.
Hold sighting-reports in the authority inbox; do not fan them out to all enrolled devices.
Delay any public non-profit bulletin until after the coordinating unit marks the sighting as acted-on or expired.

decompositions.loss: The recovered child is filmed, identified, and the still circulates on social media.
decompositions.req: After recovery, the child's face from ChildFind stills is not available to the general public.

assumptions.text: Officers and reviewers do not screenshot the inbox.
assumptions.why_fragile: They will.

assumptions.text: Drivers never see a high-resolution crop they can share.
assumptions.why_fragile: If we prompt drivers to confirm, they see the face.

assumptions.text: News media cannot FOIA the stills in identifiable form.
assumptions.why_fragile: Public-records law varies and is unsettled here.

specifications.text: Watermark reviewer stills and disable download by default; store access logs per still.
On case-closed, delete or irreversibly blur face crops in all ChildFind stores.
If a driver confirmation UI exists, show a time-limited low-resolution thumbnail that cannot be screenshotted via OS flags where available.

decompositions.loss: Search resources chase a lookalike while the actual child is moved elsewhere.
decompositions.req: A false sighting does not cause the only available officers in the true vicinity to leave that vicinity.

assumptions.text: Dispatch has more than one unit and will not redeploy the last local unit on a low-confidence pin.
assumptions.why_fragile: Rural areas have one unit.

assumptions.text: Confidence scores correspond to real-world chance it is the child.
assumptions.why_fragile: Face scores are poorly calibrated, especially for children.

assumptions.text: Multiple independent pins are required before a full redeploy.
assumptions.why_fragile: Pressure to 'do something' after a ping is high.

specifications.text: Attach match_score, number of supporting frames, and 'unconfirmed' to every sighting-report shown to dispatch.
If only one unit covers the true last-known area, flag a single low-score pin as 'do not abandon last-known'.
Output a calibrated score or an explicit low-confidence band rather than a binary match bit.

decompositions.loss: The child is in view but disguised or too young for an adult-tuned face model, so no one looks at the frame.
decompositions.req: A missing young child who is visibly present and unoccluded in a participating camera's view is not overlooked solely because they are a small child rather than an adult.

assumptions.text: A face model trained mostly on adults transfers to toddlers and school-age children.
assumptions.why_fragile: It generally does not; faces and identification cues differ.

assumptions.text: Clothing, height, and companion adult are stable enough to use as a backup cue.
assumptions.why_fragile: Clothes change; the companion may be the abductor.

assumptions.text: The search photo is a recent, frontal, well-lit picture of this child.
assumptions.why_fragile: Amber packets are often old school portraits.

specifications.text: Expose a child-specific operating mode or a separate child embedding head; output match_score for the search photo under that mode.
When face match_score is below threshold but a person crop is in-scope, emit a top-k candidate still for reviewer UI rather than dropping the frame.
Let reviewers filter by clothing-color tags supplied in the search packet, not only by face score.

decompositions.loss: The child's last known location is published so precisely that a dangerous guardian finds them first.
decompositions.req: A person who is a threat to the child does not obtain a live, meter-accurate location from ChildFind.

assumptions.text: The coordinating unit has already screened which adult may receive location updates.
assumptions.why_fragile: Intake is rushed.

assumptions.text: Parents using the non-profit portal are the safe parents.
assumptions.why_fragile: Sometimes they are not.

assumptions.text: Coarse city-level public alerts are enough for the public, so precise GPS can stay inside dispatch.
assumptions.why_fragile: Product demos will show a live map.

specifications.text: Separate the parent-status feed (search active / child recovered) from the GPS-bearing sighting inbox.
Require a two-person authority acknowledgement before any GPS-bearing still is exported.
Redact GPS to a coarse geohash on any non-dispatch role.

decompositions.loss: Parents are told of 'possible sightings' that are not their child, then crash emotionally and stop trusting later true reports.
decompositions.req: Parents are not notified of a sighting unless the coordinating unit has judged it worth acting on.

assumptions.text: Parents want every ping.
assumptions.why_fragile: They say that on day one and regret it by ping ten.

assumptions.text: A reviewer is available 24/7 to filter.
assumptions.why_fragile: Volunteer capacity is bursty.

assumptions.text: Withholding unconfirmed pings will not be described as 'the company hid sightings'.
assumptions.why_fragile: It will, if a child is later found near an unpublished pin.

specifications.text: Parent-facing events are only those marked released-to-family by the coordinating unit, not raw sighting-reports.
Keep an audit log of withheld pins so a later inquiry can show they were reviewed.
Rate-limit family notifications to a configured maximum per hour.

decompositions.loss: A real nearby sighting sits in a queue while parents are told 'no new information'.
decompositions.req: When a sighting is judged actionable, the parents (or their designated liaison) hear about it before the information is stale.

assumptions.text: Someone is on duty to make the 'actionable' judgment quickly.
assumptions.why_fragile: Night and weekend gaps.

assumptions.text: The liaison phone number in the case file still works.
assumptions.why_fragile: Families in crisis change phones.

assumptions.text: Parents are in a position to hear a call (not driving, not in the air).
assumptions.why_fragile: Not always.

specifications.text: SLA-timestamp the gap between sighting ingest and released-to-family; page an on-call reviewer when the gap exceeds a threshold.
Support multiple liaison contacts and a fallback to the coordinating unit if all fail.
If the liaison is an enrolled user, deliver the released notice over the same authenticated channel as the case.

decompositions.loss: The search packet includes a home address and photos of siblings that then leak.
decompositions.req: Home address and images of children who are not the missing child do not leave the coordinating unit's custody.

assumptions.text: Intake staff will minimize the packet to one recent photo and a last-seen area.
assumptions.why_fragile: They paste the whole flyer.

assumptions.text: Enrolled dashcams never display the packet.
assumptions.why_fragile: If drivers confirm matches, they see it.

assumptions.text: Contractor training pipelines will not scrape production packets.
assumptions.why_fragile: Unless contracts forbid it and we check.

specifications.text: Search-alert schema allows only: search-id, subject photo(s), age band, clothing tags, geo-fence, expiry — no address field.
Strip EXIF and additional faces from photos before fan-out to devices.
Contractual SPEC: production search photos are not written into the fine-tune corpus.

decompositions.loss: A sibling or the searching parent is matched as the 'abductor' or as the child and is detained.
decompositions.req: Family members who are with the missing child's siblings in public are not detained solely because a ChildFind score fired on a related face.

assumptions.text: The system can tell a sibling from the subject.
assumptions.why_fragile: Often it cannot.

assumptions.text: Officers will ask a clarifying question before a stop.
assumptions.why_fragile: Fast-moving missing-child calls produce the opposite.

assumptions.text: The family is not simultaneously the suspect in the case.
assumptions.why_fragile: Sometimes they are, which needs a different protocol, not a model.

specifications.text: Allow the coordinating unit to attach do-not-confuse reference photos of siblings that suppress a sighting-report if the best match is a sibling id.
When two enrolled identities are both above threshold, output both ids rather than argmax-only.
Label such reports 'possible related-face' in the dispatch UI.

decompositions.loss: The search is quietly ended because the non-profit is flooded, and parents are not told the network is no longer looking.
decompositions.req: Parents know whether participating cameras are still being asked to search for their child.

assumptions.text: A search-id remaining 'open' in a database means devices still have the alert.
assumptions.why_fragile: Revocation can fail on offline devices.

assumptions.text: Parents interpret 'case open' as 'cameras are searching'.
assumptions.why_fragile: Those are different.

assumptions.text: Coverage maps shown to families match devices that actually acknowledged the alert.
assumptions.why_fragile: Acks never arrive from offline units.

specifications.text: Expose to the liaison a coverage statistic: count of devices that acknowledged the current search-id in the geo-fence in the last T hours.
Whenever a radio session starts, send an ack for each still-active search-id.
If ack count in the fence drops below a floor, mark the family status 'limited camera coverage' rather than 'searching'.

decompositions.loss: Dispatch burns a shift on false pins and has no unit left for a later true pin.
decompositions.req: A ChildFind notice does not cause officers to abandon a higher-priority last-known area without a human decision.

assumptions.text: A dispatcher always stands between a pin and a unit.
assumptions.why_fragile: Staffing gaps; 'auto-assign nearest unit' will be proposed.

assumptions.text: Units will wait for a confidence label they understand.
assumptions.why_fragile: A red map pin is treated as certainty.

assumptions.text: The last-known area is still the prior.
assumptions.why_fragile: Anchoring on a new ping is strong.

specifications.text: Do not emit an auto-dispatch command; emit a sighting-notice that requires an acknowledge-to-assign action.
Show last-known area and the new pin on the same map with the unconfirmed label.
Provide match_score on the notice, not a binary 'found'.

decompositions.loss: A true sighting arrives hours later, after the child has left the area.
decompositions.req: When a participating camera had the child in view, dispatch has the notice while a search of that area can still succeed.

assumptions.text: The paired phone is in the car with Bluetooth up.
assumptions.why_fragile: Phones are in houses, offices, and pockets far from parked cars.

assumptions.text: Search-alerts are already on the device before the child is seen, so matching is local.
assumptions.why_fragile: Without Internet, the alert may arrive after the footage is overwritten.

assumptions.text: Loop footage is retained long enough for a delayed alert to be applied retroactively.
assumptions.why_fragile: Cheap units keep minutes, not hours.

specifications.text: Fan out search-alerts to devices that last reported a GPS sample inside an expanded fence, not only to devices currently online.
On receiving a search-alert, run matching over retained loop footage for the alert's time window, not only over future frames.
When a radio session starts, drain the sighting-report queue before other telemetry.

decompositions.loss: A stop or search based on ChildFind is thrown out, and the case is damaged.
decompositions.req: Officers acting on a ChildFind notice can show a lawful, purpose-limited, time-bounded authorization for that search-id.

assumptions.text: An authorized search-id corresponds to a real missing-child case, not a fishing expedition.
assumptions.why_fragile: Mission creep is a stated risk.

assumptions.text: The geo-fence and expiry on the alert match the warrant or policy instrument.
assumptions.why_fragile: Copy-paste fences will be statewide 'just in case'.

assumptions.text: Device logs are admissible and complete.
assumptions.why_fragile: Offline gaps look like spoliation.

specifications.text: Persist the legal/authorization token, geo-fence, and expiry with the search-id and show them on every sighting-notice.
Refuse to run matching if the search-alert lacks expiry or authorization-id fields.
Export a chain-of-custody package: alert, device ack, still, GPS, timestamps.

decompositions.loss: The same pipeline is reused for shoplifting, immigration, or protest monitoring.
decompositions.req: Person matching on consumer dashcams is not applied to a purpose other than an authorized missing-child search.

assumptions.text: Contractual purpose limitation will be respected under political pressure.
assumptions.why_fragile: It often is not.

assumptions.text: A 'missing child' label on a packet means the subject is a child in a genuine case.
assumptions.why_fragile: Labels can be lied about.

assumptions.text: OEMs and the non-profit will walk away if purpose expands, creating a real brake.
assumptions.why_fragile: Unless revenue replaces them.

specifications.text: Hard-code the search type enum to missing-child and drop any other type at the API boundary.
Ignore search-alerts whose type field is not missing-child.
Publish an append-only audit of search-ids issued (metadata only) to the non-profit's compliance role.

decompositions.loss: Operators ignore the inbox because yesterday it was 400 low-quality stills.
decompositions.req: The coordinating unit's ChildFind inbox remains usable on a typical search day (on the order of the national Amber rate, not a continuous firehose).

assumptions.text: Thresholding will keep volume near the 1-alert/day national rate times a small match rate.
assumptions.why_fragile: If we lower threshold for recall, volume explodes locally.

assumptions.text: Reviewers will not rubber-stamp to clear the queue.
assumptions.why_fragile: They will if measured on throughput.

assumptions.text: Geographic scoping keeps a rural desk from seeing a coastal city's matches.
assumptions.why_fragile: A national inbox is simpler to build.

specifications.text: Shard the inbox by coordinating-unit geo-fence; do not show out-of-fence stills.
Cap queued candidate stills per search-id per hour and mark overflow as count-only.
Surface queue depth next to each case so coordinators see overload as a first-class status.

decompositions.loss: Traditional canvassing stops because 'the cameras would have seen them'.
decompositions.req: Investigators continue non-camera search activity even while ChildFind is active.

assumptions.text: Command staff treat ChildFind as one sensor among many.
assumptions.why_fragile: Vendors will sell it as coverage.

assumptions.text: Coverage maps are not mistaken for 'every street is enrolled'.
assumptions.why_fragile: They will be.

assumptions.text: A degraded/offline status is visible in the same UI as pins.
assumptions.why_fragile: Separate dashboards get ignored.

specifications.text: Show enrolled-device density, not just pins, on the dispatch map.
If ack coverage is below a floor, banner 'camera network not a substitute for canvass'.
Report last-seen GPS only when the device was actually matching, not when it was powered off.

decompositions.loss: A privacy scandal ends the partnership and the search capability with it.
decompositions.req: Bystanders and families do not experience a ChildFind privacy incident that becomes public during the partnership.

assumptions.text: The manufacturer will not ship a 'growth' feature that fans photos to drivers.
assumptions.why_fragile: Marketing alignment is not guaranteed.

assumptions.text: Edge partners will not advertise 'we help find kids' with customer CCTV stills.
assumptions.why_fragile: They will want the PR.

assumptions.text: A single incident will be contained by contracts.
assumptions.why_fragile: Screenshots travel faster than contracts.

specifications.text: Bind photo display to reviewer and dispatch roles; no public CDN URLs for stills.
Require the non-profit compliance role to sign off on any new output surface (driver UI, kiosk screen, parent map).
Do not show search photos or match stills on a customer-facing screen.

decompositions.loss: Donors leave after a high-profile miss that is blamed on the non-profit 'using AI'.
decompositions.req: The public description of a miss does not claim that cameras covered a place they did not.

assumptions.text: Press statements will be coordinated with coverage facts.
assumptions.why_fragile: Speed of news vs slowness of logs.

assumptions.text: The manufacturer will not claim 'citywide' in ads.
assumptions.why_fragile: They might.

assumptions.text: Families will not be used as ad testimonials while a search is open.
assumptions.why_fragile: Growth teams will ask.

specifications.text: Export a coverage-fact sheet per case (ack counts, fences, outages) to the non-profit comms role.
Block in-product prompts that ask families for testimonials until case-closed.
Consumer marketing copy in-app must pull the same coverage numbers rather than a static slogan.

decompositions.loss: Volunteer reviewers quit because the queue is mostly not-the-child stills.
decompositions.req: Volunteer review load stays within a published per-search budget the non-profit accepted.

assumptions.text: Volunteers are interchangeable and always available.
assumptions.why_fragile: They are not.

assumptions.text: Top-k stills are a small number.
assumptions.why_fragile: k grows when recall panic hits.

assumptions.text: Reviewing children's faces all day is psychologically tolerable.
assumptions.why_fragile: It may not be.

specifications.text: Enforce a per-search cap on stills sent to volunteers; overflow goes to a paid on-call role.
Show estimated remaining queue time to the volunteer before they accept a shift.
Provide a skip/escalate control so a volunteer can drop a still without it disappearing.

decompositions.loss: The company uses the non-profit's name to sell dashcams, then ships a weaker privacy mode than the partnership described.
decompositions.req: Devices advertised under the partnership actually run the same matching and retention rules the non-profit signed.

assumptions.text: One firmware train serves OEM and consumer SKUs.
assumptions.why_fragile: Low-end SKUs will strip 'expensive' deletion and ack features.

assumptions.text: The non-profit can audit production configs.
assumptions.why_fragile: Unless the contract is logo-only.

assumptions.text: Owners cannot disable deletion while leaving matching on.
assumptions.why_fragile: A 'privacy off / matching on' toggle will be requested.

specifications.text: Refuse to enable matching unless retention-limit and ack features are compiled in and healthy.
Expose a config-attestation hash per device that the non-profit can sample.
Do not offer a matching-on / deletion-off combination.

decompositions.loss: Search photos of children circulate in volunteer Slack, press, or the contractor's demo reel.
decompositions.req: A child's search photo is not available to people outside the authorized search roles.

assumptions.text: Reviewer tools block download and external share.
assumptions.why_fragile: People use phones to photograph monitors.

assumptions.text: The contractor's sales team cannot pull production examples.
assumptions.why_fragile: They will ask for 'realistic' demos.

assumptions.text: Expired searches vanish from every replica, including backups, within a stated window.
assumptions.why_fragile: Backups lag.

specifications.text: Issue short-lived, watermarked, non-downloadable still URLs bound to reviewer identity.
Production photos are not readable by the vendor's sales or research roles.
On expiry, delete photos from object storage and enqueue backup-tombstones.

decompositions.loss: A crash is attributed to a ChildFind prompt or to compute starving the vehicle electrical system.
decompositions.req: ChildFind does not present driving-relevant alerts to the driver and does not take the vehicle electrical system below the OEM's reserved budget.

assumptions.text: The dashcam is on an accessory circuit the OEM sized for it.
assumptions.why_fragile: Aftermarket installs share cigarette-lighter circuits with other loads.

assumptions.text: Infotainment will not be used as the match UI.
assumptions.why_fragile: It is the tempting place to put a big picture.

assumptions.text: Parking-mode current draw stays within the OEM spec.
assumptions.why_fragile: Always-on matching will not.

specifications.text: Honor an OEM current-budget sample; shed matching before crash-loop recording.
No video output of match crops onto infotainment while gear is not Park.
No driver-facing match UI while speed > 0, as in R-S01-3.

decompositions.loss: Press describes the car as a rolling face-recognition network; OEM cancels the SKU.
decompositions.req: Uninvolved people photographed by the car are not identified by name or persistent id as part of ChildFind.

assumptions.text: Matching runs only while a search-id is active in the car's region.
assumptions.why_fragile: A 'pre-index everyone for speed' optimization will be proposed.

assumptions.text: No gallery of embeddings is kept between searches.
assumptions.why_fragile: On-device galleries make matching cheaper.

assumptions.text: License-plate plus face fusion will not be added as a 'bonus'.
assumptions.why_fragile: It will be asked for.

specifications.text: Do not persist person embeddings across search-ids; wipe on expiry.
Do not output a name or identity other than match_score vs the current search photo.
Do not run plate recognition as part of the ChildFind path unless a separate, authorized field is present in the search-alert.

decompositions.loss: Warranty returns spike because ChildFind overheats or bricks low-end units.
decompositions.req: Low-end hardware either performs matching within thermal limits or reports itself as non-participating rather than failing.

assumptions.text: A single model will run on every SKU.
assumptions.why_fragile: It will not.

assumptions.text: Thermal throttling still leaves crash recording intact.

specifications.text: If temperature or utilization exceeds a SKU-specific limit, stop matching and emit search-degraded.

decompositions.loss: A regulator treats always-on interior/cabin matching as illegal surveillance in the car.

assumptions.text: Passengers consented because they sat down.
assumptions.why_fragile: They did not.

assumptions.text: OEM privacy mode already disables the cabin cam.
assumptions.why_fragile: Owners re-enable it for driver monitoring.

specifications.text: Bind the ChildFind matcher input to the outward camera device id only.

decompositions.loss: Dealers cannot explain the feature, so they disable it, leaving advertised coverage fictional.
decompositions.req: A car advertised as ChildFind-capable is actually enrolled or is labeled at sale as not enrolled.

assumptions.text: Enrollment happens at delivery with a real owner account.
assumptions.why_fragile: It will be skipped.

assumptions.text: A factory default of 'on' is acceptable.

assumptions.text: Dealers will not promise coverage the car does not have.
assumptions.why_fragile: They will.

specifications.text: Enrollment requires an explicit owner action after delivery; factory default is matching-off.

decompositions.loss: On-device weights are extracted from a consumer dashcam and republished.
decompositions.req: A person who buys a dashcam does not obtain a working copy of the contractor's production model weights.

assumptions.text: Hardware is a secure enclave that owners cannot dump.
assumptions.why_fragile: Dashcams are cheap and routinely rooted.

assumptions.text: A distilled on-device model has no value if stolen.
assumptions.why_fragile: It still encodes the contractor's data.

assumptions.text: Matching can stay on the phone, which has a better TEE than the camera.
assumptions.why_fragile: Phones are also jailbroken; it also increases data movement.

specifications.text: Ship an on-device extractor/embedder that is not the full cloud model; keep the gallery comparison key on the coordinator if possible.
Store weights in a locked partition and refuse to export them over USB debug.
Watermark embeddings so a leaked model can be attributed.

decompositions.loss: Public audits show large error gaps on children or on darker skin, and the contractor is named.
decompositions.req: Disparities in whether a visible missing child is reported are not systematically associated with the child's age band or skin tone in deployed searches.

assumptions.text: Adult mugshot benchmarks predict child dashcam performance.
assumptions.why_fragile: They do not.

assumptions.text: Low-light robustness advertised by the contractor covers streetlights and headlights equally across skin tones.
assumptions.why_fragile: It often does not.

assumptions.text: We can collect child dashcam labels legally.
assumptions.why_fragile: Children's data is specially protected.

specifications.text: Report match_score distributions sliced by age-band and lighting tags on a sealed evaluation set, not only a single AUC.
Log (search-id, age-band, lighting-tag, match_score, reviewer-decision) for disparity review, without storing extra identity.
Attach a lighting/quality tag to each crop so slices are possible.

decompositions.loss: Latency or downtime of a cloud Rekognition-like path misses the useful window.
decompositions.req: A sighting is not lost solely because a cloud inference endpoint was slow or unreachable.

assumptions.text: On-device or on-phone inference is always available as fallback.
assumptions.why_fragile: Low-end SKUs cannot run it.

assumptions.text: Cloud batching is fine because searches are rare.
assumptions.why_fragile: When a search is on, latency still matters.

assumptions.text: The contractor's SLA includes dashcam-like blur and night frames.
assumptions.why_fragile: Their SLA may be clean studio images.

specifications.text: Run local matching when a search-alert is present; do not block on a cloud round-trip.
If local matching is incapable, queue crops and retry cloud inference without dropping the GPS/time that makes the report a sighting.
Expose an offline SDK path, not only a hosted API.

decompositions.loss: Fine-tuning uses photos the contractor had no license to train on, and a lawsuit lands on both companies.
decompositions.req: A child's photo provided for a live search is not used to train or advertise a model.

assumptions.text: Default cloud settings do not log production images into a training bucket.
assumptions.why_fragile: Many hosted APIs do, unless contracted off.

assumptions.text: Fine-tune infrastructure the manufacturer operates is isolated from the vendor's other customers.
assumptions.why_fragile: Shared GPUs and datasets are cheaper.

assumptions.text: Expired search photos cannot be recovered from experiment trackers.
assumptions.why_fragile: Weights-and-biases style tools hoard samples.

specifications.text: API option and default: do not persist request images; return only scores.
Manufacturer-operated fine-tune jobs read only a licensed corpus, never the live search-alert store.
Block experiment-tracker uploads of search-alert images at the gateway.

decompositions.loss: The contractor is subpoenaed as the 'face recognition company' for every ChildFind case.
decompositions.req: The contractor does not receive a copy of every production video frame, only what the manufacturer must send to meet a specified inference path.

assumptions.text: On-device inference means the vendor never sees production frames.
assumptions.why_fragile: Updates and 'helpdesk' uploads will reintroduce them.

assumptions.text: A subpoena to the manufacturer is enough for courts.
assumptions.why_fragile: Plaintiffs will sue everyone in the chain.

assumptions.text: Support logs can be sampled without full video.
assumptions.why_fragile: Engineers will ask for the clip.

specifications.text: Default inference path keeps frames on-device; cloud path sends crops not full video.

Separate the manufacturer case file from any vendor ticket so a vendor subpoena does not automatically include GPS trails.

decompositions.loss: A bystander's face is embedded and kept so they can be re-identified after the search ends.
decompositions.req: A person who is not the subject of an authorized search is not assigned a persistent identity from ChildFind processing.

assumptions.text: We only compare to one search photo, so we are not identifying bystanders.
assumptions.why_fragile: Comparison still detects and embeds every face.

assumptions.text: Embeddings without names are not identifications.

assumptions.text: People in public have no remaining biometric expectation.
assumptions.why_fragile: Regulators disagree, especially for children bystanders.

specifications.text: Do not store embeddings except the current search photo's embedding and in-memory crops of the current matching window.

decompositions.loss: A still of a bystander at a clinic, shelter, or protest is later reused in another investigation.
decompositions.req: ChildFind stills are not available to reuse for a purpose other than the originating missing-child search.

assumptions.text: Retention limits will be honored by every agency copy.

assumptions.text: The original crash-evidence recording is a separate store with its own warrant process.

assumptions.text: Edge kiosks do not keep a longer archive than the car.
assumptions.why_fragile: Centralizing makes longer retention tempting.

specifications.text: Bind every still to a search-id and refuse API access with a different purpose token.
Do not provide a free-text 'search all historical stills' endpoint.
Purge cached clips on the same expiry as the car; no partner-side archive.

decompositions.loss: People avoid streets, schools, or clinics known to be dense with enrolled cars.
decompositions.req: The public is not given a live map of which cars are currently matching faces.

assumptions.text: Coverage maps for dispatch will stay inside the authority UI.

assumptions.text: A blinking LED on the dashcam is not a usable tracker of matching state.

assumptions.text: Journalists will not scrape enrollment density from leaked APIs.
assumptions.why_fragile: They will try.

specifications.text: Public stats, if any, are delayed and aggregated at city level, not live car pins.
Do not show other users' enrollment on a map.
Do not advertise matching-active over Bluetooth beyond the paired phone.

decompositions.loss: A child bystander's face is enrolled into a gallery 'to improve child recall' without a parent.
decompositions.req: Children who are not the missing child are not added to any biometric gallery from dashcam footage.

assumptions.text: We can use crash-loop video as extra child training data because the owner consented.
assumptions.why_fragile: The child bystander did not.

assumptions.text: Blurred or synthetic children are enough to improve recall.
assumptions.why_fragile: May be true; should be tried before harvesting.

assumptions.text: Parents of bystanders will opt in via a public campaign.
assumptions.why_fragile: Response rates will be tiny and biased.

specifications.text: Fine-tune corpora exclude unlabeled dashcam faces of minors.
No 'upload hard examples' path for non-match crops.
Reject training-ingest jobs whose source is production ChildFind crops.

decompositions.loss: An employer, landlord, or immigration officer obtains a still showing where a bystander was.
decompositions.req: A ChildFind still of a bystander is not obtainable by a private party who wants to know where that person was.

assumptions.text: Only dispatch can see stills.

assumptions.text: A still without a name cannot be linked.
assumptions.why_fragile: Reverse image search and acquaintance recognition exist.

assumptions.text: NDAs bind volunteers.
assumptions.why_fragile: NDAs do not bind screenshots.

specifications.text: Minimize faces in a crop (subject-centered) and strip background license plates where feasible before a still leaves the device.
Watermark stills with the viewer id.
Drivers who confirm a match never receive a share button or a saved copy.

decompositions.loss: A bystander is stopped because they were next to a possible match in the same frame.

assumptions.text: Officers will treat other people in the crop as scenery.
assumptions.why_fragile: They will ask 'who is that adult'.

assumptions.text: Companion identification is out of scope.
assumptions.why_fragile: Someone will add 'abductor model' later.

specifications.text: Default sighting still is a tight crop; a wider context image is available only behind a second dispatcher action.

decompositions.loss: Police stop a lookalike child in public based on a ChildFind pin.

assumptions.text: Officers treat a possible-match notice as a lead that requires corroboration, not as an identification.
assumptions.why_fragile: Missing-child calls are emotional and fast.

assumptions.text: Lookalikes are rare enough that a high threshold prevents stops.
assumptions.why_fragile: School uniforms and age bands create many lookalikes.

assumptions.text: The caregiver can immediately show the child's identity.
assumptions.why_fragile: A child may have no ID; a caregiver may not be believed.

assumptions.text: The notice is shown only to dispatch, not blasted to every patrol phone as 'FOUND'.
assumptions.why_fragile: Someone will want a push to all units.

specifications.text: Every notice is labeled 'unconfirmed possible match' and includes match_score; there is no 'FOUND' state from software alone.
Do not fan a pin to all units; send it to the coordinating desk for assignment.
Output match_score and a recommended-threshold band; do not output a binary identity claim.
Attach the search photo next to the still so a human compares before a stop is authorized.

decompositions.loss: The caregiver is arrested as an abductor because they are walking with a lookalike.
decompositions.req: An adult accompanying a child who is not missing is not arrested solely on a ChildFind possible-match.

assumptions.text: There is no abductor classifier in the system.
assumptions.why_fragile: Feature requests will add one.

assumptions.text: Officers will not treat 'adult + matching child' as kidnapping-in-progress.
assumptions.why_fragile: That is a common heuristic.

assumptions.text: The true missing-child bulletin includes whether an abductor is suspected.
assumptions.why_fragile: Sometimes it does not.

specifications.text: If the case file has no suspected-companion field, the notice UI omits any companion language.
No abductor/companion score is emitted on the ChildFind path.
Require a dispatcher note before a companion-adult description is added to a unit's assignment.

decompositions.loss: A school or store goes into lockdown because a public app showed a nearby match.

assumptions.text: There is no public match feed.

assumptions.text: Drivers will not film the stop and tag the school.
assumptions.why_fragile: They will.

assumptions.text: The non-profit will not 'partner' with school apps.
assumptions.why_fragile: It is a tempting expansion.

specifications.text: No third-party webhook for match events other than the coordinating unit.
No share-to-social control on stills or pins.
Rate-limit and watermark to make scraping a live feed unattractive.

decompositions.loss: A lookalike's photo remains associated with the case online after the true child is found.

assumptions.text: Dispatchers will mark false matches.
assumptions.why_fragile: Busy desks will not.

assumptions.text: Copies have not already left the system.
assumptions.why_fragile: They may have.

assumptions.text: The lookalike family even hears that they were in a still.
assumptions.why_fragile: Often they only hear via a stop.

specifications.text: A false-match disposition deletes or quarantines that still from family and volunteer views.
Propagate the disposition to any device that queued the same crop.
Keep a sealed audit copy only for complaint investigation, with a shorter TTL.

decompositions.loss: The lookalike child becomes afraid of cameras and of going outside.

assumptions.why_fragile: Many do not.

assumptions.text: The manufacturer is allowed to require training as a condition of API access.
assumptions.why_fragile: Agencies may refuse.

assumptions.text: The caregiver is present and calm.
assumptions.why_fragile: Not always.

Do not show the lookalike child's still to additional units after disposition.

assumptions.text: Owner consent covers bystanders in public.
assumptions.why_fragile: It generally does not.

assumptions.text: A missing-child emergency exception covers continuous embedding of everyone.

assumptions.text: Offline processing on a dashcam is not 'processing' under the statute.
assumptions.why_fragile: It still is, in many regimes.

specifications.text: Start the matcher only after a valid search-alert with expiry is stored; stop at expiry.

assumptions.text: On-device matching avoids transfer entirely.
assumptions.why_fragile: Model updates and crash dumps may still leave.

assumptions.text: Authorities will not email stills to a personal Gmail.
assumptions.why_fragile: They will.

specifications.text: Pin inference and storage to a region field on the search-id.
Block fan-out to a device whose last country code is outside the case region unless an override token is present.
Prefer on-device comparison so the search photo is the only child image that must be fanned out.

decompositions.loss: Accident-evidence recordings are silently joined to a police biometric store.
decompositions.req: Crash-loop recordings made for accident evidence are not searchable as a biometric database.

assumptions.why_fragile: ChildFind will be pitched as skipping that.

assumptions.text: Owners understand they can still export a crash clip without enrolling in matching.
assumptions.why_fragile: UX may bundle them.

specifications.text: ChildFind matcher reads frames in RAM; it does not index the crash-loop archive by face.

Crash export and ChildFind enrollment are separate toggles.

decompositions.loss: A subject cannot find out whether they were matched, or get deletion, because the system is opaque.

assumptions.text: We can authenticate that the requester is the person in the still without collecting more biometrics.

assumptions.text: Offline devices will honor deletion when they next connect.
assumptions.why_fragile: Some never will.

assumptions.text: Law-enforcement copies are in scope of the same deletion.
assumptions.why_fragile: Often they are not.

specifications.text: After case-closed, expose a deletion/status request keyed by search-id to the liaison and to a DPA portal.
On receiving a delete(search-id) message, wipe queued stills and ack.
Track outstanding device acks for deletion and report incomplete deletion as a compliance status.

decompositions.loss: A precedent is set that any emotional child-safety story justifies biometric scanning of a city.
decompositions.req: Each search remains individually authorized, time-bounded, and geographically bounded rather than becoming a standing scan of all enrolled cameras.

assumptions.text: Rarity of alerts will keep political appetite limited.

assumptions.text: Geo-fences will stay tight around last-seen areas.
assumptions.why_fragile: Statewide fences are easier.

assumptions.text: Expiry will be short.
assumptions.why_fragile: Nobody will want to be the person who expired a search one hour too soon.

specifications.text: Require geo-fence + expiry on every search-id; default expiry is short and renewal is an explicit action.
Ignore alerts with empty fences or with expiry in the past.
Alert if a fence exceeds a configurable area or a renewal count exceeds a policy cap.

decompositions.loss: Customers treat the station as a surveillance site and stop coming.

assumptions.why_fragile: A camera on a pole will not.

assumptions.text: Staff will not watch stills on a back-office monitor.
assumptions.why_fragile: They will if we give them a UI.

specifications.text: Accept only encrypted sighting-report queues from authenticated dashcams; do not run a site-wide camera into the matcher.

Do not list partner sites on a public 'coverage map'.

decompositions.loss: A child was at the pump and not reported; the station is sued for hosting the system.

assumptions.text: The kiosk is not a camera.
assumptions.why_fragile: Press photos will show a camera-looking box.

assumptions.text: Contracts shift duty to the manufacturer.
assumptions.why_fragile: Plaintiffs still name the deep pocket they can find.

assumptions.text: Only enrolled cars offload, so most forecourt visitors are irrelevant.

specifications.text: Broadcast a machine-readable 'offload only, no site matching' capability flag.

decompositions.loss: Someone uses the kiosk network to pull faces of all customers.
decompositions.req: The partner network cannot be queried for people who did not just offload an enrolled dashcam queue.

assumptions.text: The kiosk has no camera and no disk of faces.

assumptions.text: Physical access to the box does not yield keys.
assumptions.why_fragile: Gas-station closets are not data centers.

assumptions.why_fragile: They will want one for 'support'.

specifications.text: Forward-only: decrypt-at-coordinator; the kiosk stores opaque blobs with TTL.

decompositions.loss: The kiosk is stolen or smashed and stored blobs are taken.
decompositions.req: Theft of a kiosk does not disclose identifiable stills or search photos.

assumptions.text: TTL is short enough that a stolen disk is empty.

assumptions.text: Drivers notice the budget UI.
assumptions.why_fragile: They are busy.

specifications.text: In fleet mode, require a fleet-paid network identity or a pre-set budget bound to the organization, not the driver's personal default.
Prefer kiosk/Wi-Fi offload on fleet vehicles.
Billable-byte reports go to the fleet org, not to the driver email.
